sections.content:
1. Introduction to statistical inference
- Some MATH2411/2421 stuff
- Some terminologies

 Terminologies were examined in the final exam as MCQ

2. Theoretical properties of (large-n) sample mean and sample variance
- Chi-Square, student's t distribution
- Multivariate Normal Distribution
- WLLN (Weak law of large numbers)
- CLT (Central Limit Theorem)
- Convergence in Probability / Distribution
- CMT (Continuous Mapping Theorem)
- Slutsky's lemma

 Remember to verify assumptions before using each theorem! (Positive and finite variance for Levy Lindeberg CLT, finite E(X⁴) for sample variance converging in probability to population variance)

 Final asked for the result of bivariate normal distribution of sample mean and sample variance of large-n normal distribution, which is in the lecture notes.

3. Point Estimation & Interval Estimation
- MME and its large-n distribution
- MLE and its large-n distribution
- Properties of estimators

 The part about distribution is the most complicated but very useful. Make sure you understand it clearly before attending the exams

 Unbiasedness & Consistency was examined, include their definition in cheatsheet

4. Bootstrapping
- Non-parametric bootstrapping

 Actually got examined but I didn't included in the cheatsheet 🤡 Forgot to use the quantile of (θ* - θ^) and just used the quantile of θ* instead

5. Hypothesis Testing
- MATH2411 stuff
- Likelihood Ratio Test
- Wilk's Test (the one using chi-sq)

 Dr. Yu specifically wants us to write the meaning of (not) rejecting H0: actual value θ is (not) significantly larger/smaller/different from θ_0. This setence was worth 5/60 points in the final.

UVMVE was excluded this semester, the overall pace is reasonable.
Not many topics actually, but man they are not easy.
sections.teaching:
Dr. Yu is passionate about teaching and teaches quite clearly (despite his heavy HK accent, and a lot of ok's) He is quite nice and humerous I think, students flock to ask him questions after lectures.

Recordings are usually uploaded a day or two after each class.  But you do miss the supplementary notes if you don't attend the physical lectures.

An final revision exercise with 6 questions was given, with solution discussed in detail in 2 lectures, but I guess that's not really enough.
sections.grading:
Very stressful grading scheme ☠️

20% 2 Assignments (10% each)
- Question 1's are the most difficult, usually proving something mentioned in the lecture
- 4 to 5 questions each
- Use Deepseek when necessary, most of the time is spent understanding the response

80% Final Exam
- Much easier this semester?
- 12 points MCQ, in which I lost 3 marks here lmao
- 4 points definitions of WLLN, CMT, -d-> and -p->
- 6 points distribution of large-n sample mean and variance of normal distribution, no proof needed (4 of the 6 blanks are 0)
- 8 points about unbiasedness, consistency, etc.
- 20 points MME and Hypothesis Testing
- 10 points MLE and Bootstrapping

One A4 double-sided *handwritten* cheatsheet allowed
Remember to include pdf / pmf / cdf / mgf / indepedent sum results (e.g. geometric sums to exponential) / mean / variance of all taught distributions

Quite messy. He jumps in between lecture notes, and suddenly introduces concepts without motivation. It takes time to digest what he is talking about.

He also is obsessed with some trivial terminology, for example small x for actual value and large X for random variable (which I think is fine), and the exact meaning of (not) rejecting H0. In the exam he gave 5 out of 60 marks for such a question and required us to include the term "not significantly/insignificantly" or else we get 0 mark. What the fuck

Remark: he says "ok" more than 700 times per lecture. I got too bored during lecture and manually counted it.

sections.content:
Chapter 1: Preliminary
Population and sample moments, moment generating function, central limit thm, delta method
Multivariate normal distribution, relationships between normal distribution and chi square distribution, t distribution and f distribution
Chapter 2: Parameter Estimation
Method of moment estimation, maximum likelihood estimation, fisher information
Chapter 3: UMVUE
Sufficient statistic, Fisher-Neyman factorization thm, complete statistic, Rao-Blackwell thm, Lehmann-Scheffe thm, exponential family and Cramer-Rao lower bound
Chapter 4: Hypothesis Testing
The grand process of hypothesis testing, likelihood ratio test, large sample test, power function of a test, uniform most powerful test, Neyman-Pearson lemma, monotone likelihood ratio, Karlin-Rubin thm.

Its quite a lot of things for a 3-cred course. The big idea of this course is when we collect a sample of data and we treat each of these sample data X_i is a random variable generated from a distribution (normal, exponential, etc.). a parameter is the value that governs the distribution (e.g. the mu and sigma^2 in normal, p in Bernoulli, and the starting point and end point of uniform distribution). The whole course is about how we use collected samples for make a guess on the parameters of distribution, and this guess is called estimator of the parameter (usually a function of random samples). The goal is to find a uniformly minimum variance unbiased estimator, which is the best estimator for the parameter and that’s what all ch2 and 3 talks about.
Ch4 talks about how we can test certain statements regarding the value of parameter using the samples collected. And how can find the best test (the uniformly most powerful test) which has the greatest probability of rejecting the null hypothesis when the null is wrong among all other tests.
sections.teaching:
To be honest, ycw isn’t that bad as I thought, his explanation is clear and I can see he is trying to use some drawing to make the lesson and notes more fun. Also, for some hard topics which require a bit tricks to solve, for example in ch3 he found many ppl have trouble find the UMVUE, he lists out some strategies of finding UMVUE for you to approach the problem under different situations. And when some chapter ends, he will give a mind map on how to solve certain problem, which I think is somehow useful for qs in mt and final.

The main thing I am not very happy with is the release of materials. The instructor likes to only release an incomplete lecture note on canvas and need u to fill in the missing part by copying down his writing during the lecture and sometimes he will release some additional hardcopy in class. Sampling from the normal distributions; maximum likelihood estimation (MLE); properties of MLE; unbiased estimation; Fisher Information; CR lower inequality; likelihood-ratio tests.

After this course, students are expected to

understand the main concept of doing statistical inference.
be able to find the maximum likelihood estimator in some statistical problems,
understand the new inferential ideas like Fisher information and CR lower bound clearly,
be able to find different estimates with some special estimation techniques they learn in class, and
be able to perform a likelihood-ratio test.

To be clear, I consider YCW a good professor regarding his attitude toward teaching. It seems that he did want to teach well.

(which my foolish student brain can't reason why)  To compensate for this, he keeps saying we can ask him questions as others wrote. Third, but not least. He requires each homework to have a 10min  recorded presentation to explain your answer. Is it really necessary if I can write out my answer on the paper?

In conclusion. YCW's teaching philosophy is to maximize pain. and hope you learn something during the process.

sections.content:
This course is mainly focused on estimators and hypothesis testing. The general idea is that you have a known or limiting distribution but with unknown parameters, and you want to construct a good estimator for these parameters, e.g. MLE and UMVUE. Most of the course is centered around this idea, with some slight variation, e.g. bootstrapping for insufficient data, bayesian prior and posterior distributions.

Topics:
1. Limit Theorems
2. Bootstrapping
3. Statistical Decision Theory
4. MLE and UMVUE
5. Hypothesis Testing
6. Bayesian Statistics

sections.workload:
The assignments had 3-4 questions each, and a lot of them are recycled from previous semesters. This means that if you have a friend or senior who took this course in a previous semester, you can just copy their solutions for most of the questions. As such, the overall workload is minimal if you have source, and I barely studied until the day before the final.

The final exam was quite mechanical and the types of questions are quite standard, e.g. finding the confidence interval for a given estimator, or applying the LRT test. We were allowed to bring one double-sided cheat sheet to the exam, so you don't really need to memorize anything. There was a couple of slightly tricky question that involved the gamma distribution and its shape and rate parameters, so make sure you write all the probability distributions on your cheat sheet.

sections.content:
CAUTION: DON'T register this course if you don't need!!! All statistical techniques you need can mostly learn from other fundamental stat. courses, which are also most of the pre-requisites of other stat.-related courses. What appears in this course is just the proof or technique used to derive the materials in those 2 courses.

Brief summary:
Part 1: Introduction (Basic knowledge will be used throughout this course)
- MGF, CLT, Multivariate normal distribution, Chi-square, t, F distribution & related confidence intervals, Order statistics

Part 2: Parameter Estimation (mostly focus on point estimation)
- Methods of finding estimators (MME, MLE), CRLB, requirements for the 'best' estimator: MVUE & UMVUE

Part 3: Hypothesis Testing
- introduction to H. test, Neyman-Pearson Lemma, UMP test, Likelihood ratio test, Pearson's goodness-of-fit test

Exams are cumulative that the part 1 and the first half of part 2 are included in the midterm and the final mainly examines the remains. The understanding of concepts may be a difficulty but for the exams, they are just step-by-step stuff.
sections.teaching:
Prof. Wong is one of the good professors among the MATH department. She knows that this is a hard course for students (not for me) so she first suggested us to drop this course if you couldn't handle with what is taught in the add-drop period. Meanwhile, she demonstrated examples and explanations with details by hand-writing. I think this teaching strategy is more appropriate than just speaking with a monotone and powerpoints in a math course teaching proofs.
She is also kind for the students who want to ask for help. Just ask her if you can't understand the materials.

However, the speed may be a little bit slow since she has to make sure we can all understand the examples and the concepts. Attendance somehow is needed because she will only upload the hand-writing notes to who attend the lectures, and you may not able to get the full picture just from the notes.

Maybe since I skipped rather many lectures, especially after the midterm, it always took me 2-3 nights to finish each assignment and prepare for the classwork. The exams also cost a lot of time to do the revision because each contains many formulae, procedures, theorems in the lecture notes.

In addition, please remember that you will take this course, together with MATH 3033 Real Analysis, a "hell" for most of the MATH student, in the fall term of your 3rd year for the SF-track, so take care of your grades.

sections.content:
分3個chapters - introduction (mainly MATH 2421啲野，亦有新野 = delta method, order statistics), estimation（點樣揾一個好既unbiased estimator）, hypothesis testing（MATH 2411有簡單提過，但係完全唔係同一層次）。
Midterm考到Section 2.3 (=Cramer-Rao Lower Bound)，Chapter 2雖然睇起上嚟好複雜但係做熟咗會覺得易，但係Chapter 3既likelihhod ratio test簡直噩夢級……
sections.teaching:
教得好唔好呢就見仁見智啦（參見secret討論）。
Prof Wong係會上堂一路講一路寫notes，講都算清楚既，但係有時都要之後睇翻手寫notes先會明。
不過佢會好樂意落堂/office hour解答你既疑難，同埋會認得你既樣+名
sections.grading:
Stat course通常都有2種scheme，呢個都唔例外。
5% Homework（total 6份）
5% Classwork（total 3次，其實即係quiz）
25% / 35% Midterm
65% / 55% Final
Prof Wong都出名fail多人（如果你真係差到佢接受唔到），不過勝在有2種scheme起碼俾你可以final追翻 / midterm保底。
Overall mean = 60.22, s.d. = 22.01, above mean差唔多1個s.d. ⇒ A-
sections.workload:
相比起其他淨係midterm+final既MATH course係會多咗好多野做，但係homework同classwork啲題型同exam相近（e.g. midterm第一題淨係改咗啲數字），當係平時溫咗書囉。
Professor仲會有additional既exercise俾大家做，建議做埋佢，尤其係Chapter 3，會令你明翻少少（雖然我final都係唔識orz）。
順便一提classwork係tuto嗰陣做，佢會事先send email通知大家有，其餘時間走曬tuto無問題。
同埋因為佢會堂上點名（not for attendance/paticipation，純粹跟張list send翻手寫notes），所以最好堂堂上。
（打完好似好大workload咁，個人幾中意stat所以覺得還好，如果淨係想fulfill elective又無乜興趣就唔好take啦）

sections.content:
哩個course主要係講2411同2421學過既野，背後既concept，如果唔記得曬2421 D野，一開始上堂會完全唔知佢講咩
FINAL 有一半考既野好STANDARD，同PASTPAPER既野差唔多一樣，但其實唔明，就咁死背既話都未必識做
如果你係想min精算所以讀哩個COURSE，我建議你讀其他，因為哩個COURSE 真係好煩
